[1, 2], the macro-micro modeling approach starts with a finite element macroscopic sample scale model, e.g. the macro-model. After the macro-model simulations, the most critical region will be identified which will be used for the micro-model. 4.3.1 The macro-models The macro-models for 3-P bending and clinch test are two dimensional and they are shown exactly as in Fig. 3 and Fig. 5. As for the 3-P bending model, plane strain is assumed. The rollers and punch blade are represented by rigid body surfaces. The aural-5 are modeled as isotropic elastic-plastic deformable body and is represented with 4-noded plane strain rectangular meshes with reduced integration (CPE4R). Fine meshes were utilized at the center region with a mesh size of 0.02×0.02 mm2 (see Fig. 8(a)) For the clinch test, axis-symmetry is assumed. The holders and the punch are represented by rigid body surfaces, while 4-noded axisymmetric mesh is used to mesh aural-5 plate. Fine meshed were used at the region of punch edge with a mesh size the same as that of the 3-P bending model (see Fig. 8(b)). (a) (b) Fig. 8. The fine mesh regions of the macro-models of 3-P bending (a) and clinch test (b). The isotropic elastic properties of the plate include the Young’s modulus of 70GPa and Poisson’s ration of 0.33, which are typical for Al alloys. The tension test results are used to provide the flow behavior of aural-5 as-cast and e-coated alloy in the macroscopic model. For this purpose, one of these curves each for the as-cast and e-coated alloy was used. Firstly, the engineering stress-strains is converted into a true (logarithm) stress-strain curve [3]. Then the elastic part of the strain is removed, and plastic part of the curve is used.
